subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw change memory_search chunking to respect Markdown headings by default, add an opt-in chunking strategy/config, or defer chunking until the broader Memory MVP/entity design is settled?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the implementation changes persisted index identity and retrieval behavior, and the issue also bundles a larger entity/graph-memory direction that automation should not choose.

options.title: Approve A Narrow Chunking Design
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

options.title: Make Heading-Aware The Default
options.body: Adopt heading boundaries as canonical Markdown memory behavior, accepting that existing headed files will reindex and retrieve differently.

options.title: Defer To Memory MVP
options.body: Wait for memory write/entity pipeline decisions so chunking, extraction, and wiki synthesis land as one coordinated design.

recommendation.title: Approve A Narrow Chunking Design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, implement heading-aware chunking as a focused memory-core change with explicit reindex semantics, and track entity extraction separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The immediate unresolved choice is the core memory chunking, config/default, and index-identity contract, which traces most strongly through steipete's feature-history work.
